about: Environment rules per disease class (docs/DISEASE_RULES.md). Every rule cites an opened source; every rule is a draft until an agronomist reviews docs/RULES_REVIEW.csv. Explanation only: never changes a diagnosis.

tmean.label: mean daily temperature
tmean.meaning: mean of the daily mean air temperature over the window

tmin.label: mean daily minimum temperature
tmin.meaning: mean of the daily minimum air temperature over the window

tmeanMin.label: coldest daily mean temperature
tmeanMin.meaning: lowest daily mean air temperature in the window

rhMean.label: mean relative humidity
rhMean.meaning: mean of the daily mean relative humidity over the window

wetDays.label: wet days
wetDays.meaning: days in the window with at least `hours` hours at RH >= 90% (leaf-wetness proxy, Sentelhas et al. 2008, docs/DISEASE_RISK.md); hourly weather only

soil.ph.label: soil pH
soil.ph.meaning: soil pH: the farmer's Soil Health Card if entered, else SoilGrids pH (H2O), 0-30 cm, modelled

soilTest.availableN.label: Soil Health Card available N
soilTest.availableN.meaning: available N (alkaline permanganate), Soil Health Card only

soilTest.availableP.label: Soil Health Card available P
soilTest.availableP.meaning: available P (Olsen), Soil Health Card only

soilTest.availableK.label: Soil Health Card available K
soilTest.availableK.meaning: available K (ammonium acetate), Soil Health Card only

soilTest.ocPct.label: Soil Health Card organic carbon
soilTest.ocPct.meaning: organic carbon (Walkley-Black), Soil Health Card only

soilTest.zn.label: Soil Health Card zinc
soilTest.zn.meaning: DTPA zinc, Soil Health Card only

soilTest.fe.label: Soil Health Card iron
soilTest.fe.meaning: DTPA iron, Soil Health Card only

soilTest.s.label: Soil Health Card sulphur
soilTest.s.meaning: available sulphur, Soil Health Card only

season.label: season
season.meaning: calendar season of the reference date (see seasons)

seasons.note: Months shared by two seasons in the source (October, March) belong to both. This is the calendar season, not the crop's own sowing date, and not district-specific.

source.title: Cropping seasons of India - Kharif & Rabi
source.publisher: Indian Economic Service (Arthapedia), Government of India
source.quote_or_numbers: The kharif cropping season is from July –October during the south-west monsoon and the Rabi cropping season is from October-March (winter). The crops grown between March and June are summer crops.

source.title: Soil Health Card Scheme (PIB release PRID 1808329)
source.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
source.quote_or_numbers: soil testing can be repeated after a time gap of two years after first testing

classes.cause: grain discoloration by Alternaria, Bipolaris (Cochliobolus) sativus, Cladosporium and other fungi

sources.title: Black Point of Wheat
sources.publisher: Crop Protection Network (US land-grant universities extension)
sources.quote_or_numbers: Warm, wet weather during filling and ripening (FGS 10.5) typically favors infection, but black point can also be prevalent if weather is hot and dry.

classes.no_rule_reason: The sources give only qualitative and contradictory weather (warm-wet, but also hot-dry) and no thresholds; the symptom forms on grain at filling/ripening, which a 14-day weather window cannot place.

classes.cause: Fusarium spp. (F. culmorum, F. pseudograminearum and others) root, crown and foot rot

sources.title: Fusarium Root, Crown, and Foot Rot of Wheat
sources.publisher: Crop Protection Network (US land-grant universities extension)
sources.quote_or_numbers: Seedling blight is favored when seed is sown into dry, warm (68-86°F) soil. Dry weather typically favors Fusarium root, crown, and foot rot, but infection can occur under a wide range of environmental conditions.

classes.no_rule_reason: The only numbers (20-30 °C soil) are for soil at sowing, which the snapshot does not have; the rest is qualitative ('dry weather typically favors').
Healthy class: no disease rules.

classes.cause: spot blotch, Bipolaris sorokiniana (the main cause of leaf blight of wheat in India)

rules.reading: The source's 'more than 12 to 18 hours of leaf wetness' is read as at least one day with 12 h at RH >= 90% in the last 7 days.

sources.title: Chowdhury AK, Singh G, Tyagi BS, Ojha A, Dhar T, Bhattacharya PM (2013). Spot blotch disease of wheat – a new thrust area for sustaining productivity. Journal of Wheat Research 5(2). doi:10.25174/3pfz0r92
sources.publisher: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (journal); Uttar Banga Krishi Vishwavidyalaya
sources.quote_or_numbers: Ideal conditions … relative humidity of near 95 per cent … and long periods (more than 12 to 18 hours) of leafs wetness (p. 1). Moderate to warm temperature range (18˚C to 32˚C) favours the growth of B. sorokiniana (p. 3).

classes.cause: Magnaporthe oryzae pathotype Triticum (reported in Bangladesh 2016; not established in India)

rules.reading: Tmin and Tmax for infection (hourly in the model) applied to the daily mean.

sources.title: Montes C, Hussain SG, Krupnik TJ (2022). Variable climate suitability for wheat blast (Magnaporthe oryzae pathotype Triticum) in Asia. International Journal of Biometeorology 66:2237-2249. doi:10.1007/s00484-022-02352-9
sources.section_or_page: Methods, infection model (parameters from Cruz et al. 2016)
sources.quote_or_numbers: T min = 10 °C, T max = 32 °C, and T opt = 27.5 °C … WD min and WD max (hours), taken as 12 and 24, respectively … the minimum and maximum leaf wetness duration requirement for infection

sources.title: Bacterial blight (fact sheet)
sources.quote_or_numbers: In general, the disease favors temperatures at 25−34°C, with relative humidity above 70%. … Bacterial blight can be severe in susceptible rice varieties under high nitrogen fertilization.

sources.title: Yoshino (1979) infection hours as published in Katsantonis et al. (2017), with Padmanabhan (1965) as supporting evidence
sources.quote_or_numbers: 5-day mean 20–25 °C, rain < 4 mm/h, wet run >= base wet hours + 4 h; daily infection hours < 3 low, 3–5 medium, >= 6 high

classes.cause: Bipolaris oryzae (Cochliobolus miyabeanus); common on nutrient-deficient soils

sources.title: Brown spot (fact sheet)
sources.quote_or_numbers: The disease can develop in areas with high relative humidity (86−100%) and temperature between 16 and 36°C. It is common in unflooded and nutrient-deficient soils

classes.no_rule_reason: Healthy class: no disease rules.

classes.cause: rice tungro bacilliform and spherical viruses, spread by green leafhoppers

sources.title: Tungro (fact sheet)
sources.section_or_page: What it does; Why and where it occurs
sources.quote_or_numbers: Rice tungro disease is caused by the combination of two viruses, which are transmitted by leafhoppers.

classes.no_rule_reason: Vector-borne virus: the source gives no weather or soil threshold for the disease itself.

classes.cause: cold injury (physiological disorder) after a sudden temperature drop

rules.reading: The reported 2.7–7 °C daily means are read as at least one day with a mean of 7 °C or less; 14 days because the bands show weeks after the cold (Texas handbook).

sources.title: Singh SP, Vishwakarma SK, Singh SP, Singh A, Sharma BL (2017). Novel report of banded chlorosis in commercial sugarcane cultivars from sub-tropical India. Int J Curr Microbiol App Sci 6(4). doi:10.20546/ijcmas.2017.604.044
sources.publisher: Sugarcane Research Institute, UP Council of Sugarcane Research, Shahjahanpur
sources.quote_or_numbers: The symptoms were highly appeared at the average temperature of 5.25 0 C with the range from 2.7 to 7 0 C in last week of January, 2016.

sources.title: Sugarcane
sources.publisher: Texas Plant Disease Handbook, Texas A&M AgriLife Extension
sources.quote_or_numbers: It occurs as a result of cold damage to portions of unrolled leaves within the spindle. The damage is visible weeks later, when the leaves grow out.

rules.reading: 'Night temperature' is read as the daily minimum.

sources.title: Sanjel S, Chaulagain B, Small IM, Comstock JC, Hincapie M, Raid RN, Rott P (2019). Comparison of progress of brown rust and orange rust and conditions conducive for severe epidemic development during the sugarcane crop season in Florida. Plant Disease 103:825-831. doi:10.1094/PDIS-05-18-0862-RE
sources.quote_or_numbers: Maximum disease severity was correlated with the number of hours at night with an average temperature of 20 to 22.2°C … Epidemics of brown rust began at lower night temperatures (16.7 to 22.2°C)

sources.title: Selvakumar R, Viswanathan R (2019). Sugarcane rust: changing disease dynamics and its management. Journal of Sugarcane Research 9(2):97-118. doi:10.37580/JSR.2019.2.9.97-118
sources.quote_or_numbers: In India, the rust severity is restricted to peninsular regions … and sub tropical states are relatively free from rust diseases due to unfavourable climate for rust pathogens.

sources.title: Viswanathan R (2018). Changing scenario of sugarcane diseases in India since introduction of hybrid cane varieties: path travelled for a century. Journal of Sugarcane Research 8(1)
sources.quote_or_numbers: foliar diseases such as rust, brown spot, eye spot, brown stripe, pokkah boeng etc were reported during different periods … the foliar diseases were seasonal in occurrence and mostly variety specific.

classes.no_rule_reason: No field weather threshold found (only 'seasonal' and 'high humidity areas'; the one number found is an in-vitro growth optimum of 25 °C).

classes.cause: dried leaves: a symptom with several possible causes (drought, senescence, disease)
classes.no_rule_reason: The dataset class is a symptom, not one cause, so no single rule applies.

classes.cause: sugarcane grassy shoot phytoplasma, spread by infected setts and insect vectors

sources.quote_or_numbers: Treat the setts with aerated steam at 50°C for 1 hour to control primary infection … spraying twice a month with aphidicides

classes.no_rule_reason: Phytoplasma spread by setts and vectors: no weather or soil threshold in the sources.
Healthy class: no disease rules.

classes.cause: Fusarium species complex (F. sacchari, F. proliferatum, F. verticillioides and others)

rules.reading: '70–80%' (most severe) and '79.0–85.5%' (incidence) are read as a lower bound of 70%.

sources.title: Poorniammal R, Jernisha J, Prabhu S, Dufossé L (2024). Sugarcane Pokkah Boeng disease: insights and future directions for effective management. Life 14:1533. doi:10.3390/life14121533
sources.quote_or_numbers: The disease was most severe when temperatures ranged from 20 °C to 32 °C, accompanied by high humidity levels of 70–80% and cloudy weather during the rainy season, particularly from July to September.

sources.title: Pokkah boeng
sources.quote_or_numbers: Pokkah boeng was favoured by warm, moist condition and additionally, summer showers with cloudy weather also favour disease development

sources.title: Sett rot
sources.quote_or_numbers: Proper drainage and planting of setts in 1-2 cm depth … Avoid deep planting during monsoon season

classes.no_rule_reason: Only qualitative (drainage, planting depth in the monsoon); no threshold.

classes.cause: sugarcane viral diseases (the dataset class does not name the virus)
classes.no_rule_reason: Generic class without a named virus; viral diseases spread by setts and vectors, not by weather thresholds.

sources.title: Reddy MV, Raju TN, Sharma SB, Nene YL, McDonald D (1993). Handbook of pigeonpea diseases. Information Bulletin no. 42
sources.section_or_page: Cercospora Leaf Spot (pdf p. 26); Phyllosticta Leaf Spot (pdf p. 30)
sources.quote_or_numbers: Cercospora: Cool temperatures (25°C) and humid weather favor the disease. Phyllosticta: Mean temperatures ranging from 20 to 30°C with a mean humidity range of 73-80% favor severe outbreaks.
